label: input token y
explanation: Single-token detector: fires on exactly every step whose input token is the letter y, in both the original and copy phases (dev P=R=F1=1.0, correlation 0.99). It never fires on any other token, including <DEL>. Magnitude is highest (about 0.81, the max) when y is the first token of the sequence (t=0). When y comes in as the first copy-phase input (t=L+1) the value is about 0.7-0.8. y at later positions gives about 0.6-0.7. Position, L, phase and the neighbouring tokens do not change whether it fires.

issues: None material. Test split: P=R=F1=1.0, mass recall 1.0, correlation 0.99. 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.
Profile matches the claims: in_tok=y is active at rate 1.000 and every other token at 0. <DEL> is never active. Firing rate is flat across t, L, phase, prev_tok and out_tok.

Magnitude claims hold roughly. Per-step mass at t=0 (mass share 0.113 over 16824 steps) is higher than at t=1 or later positions, and the top example is y at t=0 = 1.00 of max, with the copy-phase y at 0.75. These are minor secondary details.
